## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design registry-driven drift handling for multi-region data sources, ensuring per-record contracts, lineage, and robust upserts in a lakehouse.

## Key Concepts

- Central schema registry with canonical schema and versioning
- Iceberg dynamic schema evolution and region partitioning
- Per-record lineage and idempotent upserts
- Late data handling with buffering window
- Drift detection and contract testing

## Code Example

```javascript
MERGE INTO iceberg_table t
USING staging s
ON t.region = s.region AND t.id = s.id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.value = s.value, t.modified_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, region, value, modified_at) VALUES (s.id, s.region, s.value, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test the registry drift in CI/CD?
- How would you rollback a problematic schema change without breaking downstream jobs?

```sql
-- Upsert example with deduplication
MERGE INTO lake.regions.device AS target
USING staging AS src
ON target.region = src.region
   AND target.device_id = src.device_id
   AND target.ts = src.ts
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET
   target.metrics = src.metrics,
   target.updated_at = current_timestamp()
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT

```
